messages:
alex: FYI — yesterday at ~09:12 we saw ap-south GPU pool pressure spike, had to shift ~60% of inference traffic to ap-southeast. manual cutover worked but we had a couple of degraded requests for 3–4m.
priya: thanks. do we know if this was capacity exhaustion or network flakiness between AZs?
maria: logs show repeated NCCL timeout errors on node gnode-aps-014 and kernel ooms on gnode-aps-019. kube events: `PodEvicted` + `ImagePullBackOff` for a handful of nodes.
alex: my read — noisy neighbor + a bad driver rollback earlier that morning. capacity looked fine until GC/driver combo caused split brain across the MIGs.
sam: ops-bot alerted at 09:09, but runbook step for autoscale didn't trigger because `scale_policy:protected` flag was set on that pool.
ops-bot: Alert: GPU_Pool_aps_high_pressure fired (threshold: 85%) — incident created 1760823400. Automated scale attempted (2/3) and failed: quota limit in project-redwood-ap-south.
priya: can we add a preflight that checks quota before autoscale tries? we lost ~2mins with retries.
alex: agree. also need an explicit fallback path that shifts traffic in smaller increments (10% steps) and verifies health per-step.
taylor: suggested runbook patches in-line. propose to update the failover playbook with these changes:

1) Preflight checks (new):
   - verify project quotas (`gcloud compute reservations list` / AWS equivalent)
   - check driver version consistency across nodes (`kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep nvidia`) 

2) Autoscale behavior change:
   - if `scale_policy:protected` -> emit WARNING and attempt quota-bump request template instead of retrying autoscale.

3) Traffic shift procedure (replace single 100% shift):
   - Use incremental shift command:

```
# control-plane CLI
rctl traffic shift --from ap-south --to ap-southeast --step 10 --health-check /healthz --wait 30s
```

   - after each step verify 200s and p99 latency < 400ms before next increment.

4) Node remediation checklist (run in parallel):
   - cordon & drain suspect nodes: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`
   - collect NVML logs and tcpdump on infra VLAN (5m capture): `tcpdump -i eth1 -w /tmp/aps-gn-014.pcap`

5) Post-incident actions (new):
   - open driver rollback RCA with infra-research, include ddtrace spans
   - submit quota request playbook with template + oncall step to contact cloud-ops

maria: +1 on incremental shift. also add a checklist to monitor KV-cache hit rates — shifts caused cache thrash and some failed prompts.
sam: assigning owners: priya -> preflight & quota template, taylor -> update CLI and traffic shift script, alex -> node remediation docs, maria -> cache monitoring addendum.
priya: I'll draft quota template and add the preflight command snippets. ETA EOD today.
alex: I'll run the node remediation checklist against gnode-aps-014 in staging and paste results in the playbook.
taylor: I'll add the `--step` param to rctl and add a test in eng-infra CI to simulate partial shifts.
ops-bot: Action created: INCIDENT-1760823456-1 (Failover playbook updates). Owners: priya, taylor, alex, maria. Due: 1760909856.
maria: small note — add an explicit item to disable `scale_policy:protected` only via a two-person approval flow. we hit that flag accidentally.
sam: retrospective item: run cost analysis on incremental shifts vs single-shot for the last quarter. incremental may cost a bit more but reduces failed requests.
alex: ok. can someone PR the runbook by tomorrow morning? otherwise we'll be updating live notes during the next maintenance.
priya: I'll open PR to docs/runbooks/gpu-failover.md and tag @eng-sre for review.

ops-bot: Closing thread note: make sure to include the log snippets and tcpdump sample in the PR. :thumbsup:
